review_text: The lack of communication with this company will drive you insane. That's cheating sourcing technology manager is incompetent and I would advise to stay far far away from this company. Leadership needs work, Miss manage and horrible bosses. Typical work typical work day includes a ton of Miss informed meetings as well as finger pointing towards one another. You would wouldn't be surprised on the amount of turnover that this company receives, as I'm surprised it is still in business with the lack of organizational skills. Stay away

review_title: Fun and fast-paced place to work
review_text: Yelp has one of the most amazing cultures out there. That being said, cold-calling is an extremely tough job and not for the weak of heart.The hardest part of the job is undergoing constant rejection from business owners.

This is a very cut-throat position with a big emphasis on quantity over quality. They are more concerned with you hitting the 80 call and 2 1/2 hour talk time minimum, rather than the quality of your actual conversations sell. Managers are way too hands on, and micro-manage all day long. They promote managers way too quickly who were simply good at sales and not necessarily good leaders. The territories are too saturated and have a huge impact on whether you are a successful rep.

I enjoyed working with my teammates. Yelp offers great health benefits, 401k and stock options. There are some great managers. 
However culture can vary by department. My experience was not indicative of a healthy work/life balance. We had high quantitative goals that were expected to be exceeded but no incentives.
Not a lot of options for advancement.
Good company, but you are overmanaged a bit. I enjoyed woring there, but you need to make a lot of phone calls every single day. Good managers, pay is not very high
Relaxed fun environment good people to work with made many friends there.Great atmosphere there are pool tables free lunches red bull and managers are very cool.

review_title: Good for fresh out of college that's it
review_text: The company makes sure you have access to managers, great reps, and anyone that you would have to go to for help. They are able to give you thorough training and everything is fast paced.

I feel as though I've learned so much here - much more than if I went to grad school. 

My manager cares about my career and wants to see me succeed and is willing to put in the time and effort to make sure that I'm happy.

Yelp is a great place to work for a young individual who is looking for good experience. The issue I had was that they are promoting managers rapidly due to growth, and often promote people who are not capable of being good managers. It is a sales position, so expect to have sales goals, but the culture is amazing and offer a lot to younger people.

review_title: If you don't mesh with your manager ask to change teams.
review_text: Overall Yelp is a pretty nice place to work. The Chicago office is the fastest growing office of the company so if you work hard you can get promoted pretty quickly. That's where the cons come from. Some managers get promoted because they are great at sales but they aren't really fit to be leaders.

A typical day at work is 70-80 cold calls to small business owners to sell them Yelp advertising. With no sales experience, this was a great position to introduce to me sales. 

The management is hot and cold, you can feel and see how stressed most managers are. I believe this comes from the top down, and the excess pressure that is put on each person. 

The culture is great. Fully stocked kitchen, barista, kegs, pool tables, young people. Great for someone who has just graduated college and is looking to a smooth transition from college to work life.

The hardest part of the job is how mundane it is. Every day is the same, every month is the same. You come in each day, make phone calls, try and close deals, try and hit quota and then you do it all again the next month. Even though Yelp has a great product it is extremely draining talking to business owners who don't like the company.

The most enjoyable part are the people. You can distract yourself for the stressful day to day job by meeting some really great people

Yelp overall is an okay place to work. There is no perfect place to work, so you'll always have highs and lows at any job. There's lots of pressure to perform well. The sales structure is a bit stringent but the training is exceptional and they try to make the necessary tools available for employees to succeed. My biggest issue is with the young untrained management. Its great to promote from within, but without proper training is a recipe for failure, thus the extremely high turnover. There's a training class of new hires EVERY MONTH of 60-80 people.
expect way to much, hard work, so may dials, like the teams, liked my manager, the kitchen is awesome, my least favorite part was the level of micromanagement

Not worth it, management is horrible, when you have an issue with a manager and report it to HR they don't do anything to fix the issue. Managers have the ability to single you out and no one does anything about it. Hours are horrible, most of the day you spend at work and have no time to do anything else, call queue is high and eventually it wears you out. Management has strong favoritism. So if you are not a "favorite" There will be no advancement within the company. They do not have flexible hours at all. Even if you put in a request. For the hours that you spend there the lunches are 30 minutes. The good deeds are not ever appreciated. At first they make you feel welcomed but as time goes by it gets sour real fast. Don't waste your time there's other jobs that are worth the pay and time. This is not one of them.

review_title: Productive workplace with all tools needed to perform job
review_text:
Great people to work with, all Account Managers had at least a Bachelors Degree and were fun personalities.  Interesting opportunity to work for a dot-com. 

The workplace was constant high energy with music and distractions all day!

Fun place to work. Keeps you on your toes. Learned a lot about sales and good communication. Management is good when you are matched with the right person. The Culture here is relax but fast. Hardest part for me was being on the same page with my manager. She wasn't the right match for me and I tried to change manager but she never signed off on my change. Over all it wouldn't have been so hard if my manager was there to help me. Everyday was something new, the job was a joy of it's own.

review_title: Free food only plus, good for your resume
review_text: It's a cool place for getting some experience but not somewhere I would start a career. They will hire anyone to fill a spot.  No professionalism at all. From managers to customer service reps. Reasons why customers disliked the service. I wouldn't recommend working here overall.
Yelp is a great place to work! They have great managers and communication styles. Weekly one on one meetings to see how you are performing. A lot of Growth in the company as well.

review_title: Interesting atmosphere and culture but poor management
review_text: Too much time is spent attending to incidents or working around incidents from other teams. Many managers are new/first-time managers and lack the necessary skills to be effective at their jobs while others are handi-capped by the company's culture of super hands off management. Morale is generally poor-whatevs.

Each day consists of a high volume of cold calls and emails sent out to SMB owners. Management varied, with some managers just one year out of the account executive role. Issues with that were panic when things weren't going well.

review_title: Fantastic work environment//terrible at preparing you to be successful
review_text:
Similar to plenty of other reviews I have read, tons of kids fresh out of college who have no idea that there ARE better options out there. They lure you in with all the free food and music and games and stuff but dont tell you about the cold calling and if you dont hit these metrics on the head then you will be shown the door. Managers may "act" like they care about you or your home life but at the end of the day you are just a number. training structure is way out of order. They throw you to the wolves the second week on the job and then give you information in a training 2-3 weeks later that would have increased your odds of getting a appointment/sale. Lots of tasks to accomplish on a daily basis but not enough time to complete them all and then you are hit with the no excuses card when you are not pulling your weight. 


On the flip side, fantastic place to work, free food all day, game rooms and music, lots of stuff nearby.

Great for younger kids with no responsibilities!!

No one likes cold-calling, but that's what you're going to be doing every day. Yes, you get the freedom to churn the whole sales process from open calling to closing, but managing that while handling objections is a tough sell. Co-workers are friendly, and management could be held to another standard. Hard to differentiate managers as friend or micromanaging sticklers, because people move up quick in this job. It can be very emotionally draining and dry, so mentality is everything in this job.

The fun atmosphere with music, ping pong and common chatting with other employees has made Yelps culture fun. The managers are super hands on in trying to help out to ensure the growth of each employee.

start at 730 get yelled at by manager. Start cold calling, anytime you get up you get yelled at by manager to get back on phone. Make to many calls get yelled at again, make to little yelled at. Micromanaged and were put on kid teams (my team name was the queen bees).

review_title: Celebrate for your team and others around you when someone makes a sale
review_text: This is my first sale job and overall experience has been positive.You will go into training and be expected to learn and implement feedback. With each month that goes by the expectations will go up. It will seem fun in the beginning with the games, free coffee, open cafeteria, and a keg for after hours but it gets old and you just want to go home and relax. You will dial 70 + call a day and be expected to hit 2.50 hours talk time. The job can be high stress at times and if you close a deal directors, managers, and other people will cheer your wins. At times if your not closing it can feel disappointing and you feel forgotten and question if this is the job for you. Going into this job you have to have a thick skin, implement feedback, work hard, adjust to things that might not go your way because this is sales.

Typical day is about 9-10 hours with an hour lunch break. If you want to be successful you have to put some extra time into the job. Managers are great and the sales curriculum is top notch. Honestly love the company, but cold calling 65+ times a day can become taxing.

The culture at Yelp is great. Lots of perks in the office and usually everyone is cool. But managers tend to breathe down your neck and instead of working with you to get better they just tell you that you better work harder. 

There is no acknowledging that bad days happen - instead it's 100% you for not working hard enough.
Poor Pay. You are getting paid below market value. Your managers are children fresh out of college with no work experience. no opportunity for upwards growth

review_title: Great place to work. Best years of my life.
review_text:
Simply put, I love working at Yelp. The training is unparalleled, and the people are amazing. There are several upper level sales opportunities that have clear paths to get to. Unlike many other sales positions, it is unclear how to get promoted, however it seems as though all managers' goals are to get their reps promoted.

The recipe to success at this company is simple: work hard, be the obvious choice, and be a team player.  

The hardest part of this job is the work itself, however Yelp is quite clear about what our average level of work is. Cold-calling is never easy, especially when dealing with small business owners, however there are several tools at our fingertips to improve our sales acumen. As long as your goal (as a sales rep) is to genuinely help a small business, there is no reason why you wouldn't succeed. 

All in all, would highly recommend. This is one of the few companies that allows college grads to develop a lifelong career with some hard work and dedication to the role.
great place to work if you are a new grad, but for someone older, it will feel really unprofessional. Managers are inexperienced because yelp doesn't pay enough to keep employees around

review_title: Run as far as you can in the opposite direction.
review_text:
Worked here for a year as an Account Executive - they rope you in really quick. Show you videos about success stories, tempt you with other people's successes, and give you tons of free food and alcohol. They make you think this job is possible and right for everyone. Then you're thrown into the mix with little to no support from managers that are just as experienced as you are. 

There is a ridiculous clique vibe here - the people who are the top performers are all best friends, and if you're not performing at the top you can't be friends with them. They're the favorites. If you are a favorite and then start performing badly, you're all but exiled and eventually fired without much warning. If you decide to leave on your own merit, you're also exiled and lose all your friends and references due to petty management.

Aside from feeling like you're in a movie about high school with the cliques and all the bratty kids who are clearly just entertaining this sales job for fun while they wait for their parents to give them their inheritance money, the place is a frat house. 95% of the staff are dating, living together, going out drinking together, casually hooking up, and this includes management. It's nice that they encourage a close-knit-meet-your-best-friends-here environment, but it's borderline incestual. 

If you're not partaking in this weird friendship culture, again - you are alienated and not helped. They guilt trip you for missing happy hours and other drinking events because you have a life outside your job.

I would give this one star but they do have free healthcare benefits and that is the ONLY good thing about this company. 

Bottom line is that if you're looking for a starting point in sales, there are THOUSANDS of better opportunities than this place. But, if you're into drinking 24/7 with your co workers, hooking up with your co workers and managers, all while stressing about little to no training and harassing innocent small business owners (who you still have to call even if they don't speak English or respectfully decline), then Yelp is the place for you!

review_title: Very productive yet fun and young atmosphere
review_text: Took a 2-month full training course through the Yelp University sales program. Learned various sales techniques and the ins and outs of online marketing. A typical day of work consisted of vetting accounts to reach out to throughout the day, coming up with a game plan to approach a certain number of accounts in a day, and ultimately closing sales. Management was very helpful and approachable about anything. Managers successfully lead sales teams as a whole while still focusing on individuals. The hardest part of the job is the cold calling aspect, and getting small business owners to commit to and advertising program. The most enjoyable part of the job is definitely the atmosphere as food and drinks were complimentary, and Yelp provided many activities such as ping pong and mini basketball hoops.

review_title: Great work culture, young hungry employees.
review_text: Working at Yelp was a great experience and I learned a lot, however for those considering the Account Executive position, be sure that you want and are willing to make cold calls all day. It is definitely not for everyone. Managers are all people who have had the same job as you for over a year so they are really helpful and genuinely want to see you succeed.

I feel this job was truly false as far as what I felt I would be doing against what you actually do. They entice you with the whole "google" work environment, but when you get there you are just another number and you might as well be handcuffed to you manager as micro-management is over done there. The lure young ambitious college students and give them a bad taste of the work field.

a typical day starts off with enjoying free breakfast then hitting the phones. Its a typical telemarketing job with perks of free food that is all. Your co workers are nice. They know how to pick the right people for this job. But management sucks. Your suppose to call up to 120 people per day and your manager can and will listen in on your phone calls. They set unrealistic sales goals and basically try to teach you how to harass small business owners. Prior to this job I've worked in sales but working here is like being a bill collector. You will be forced to call the same businesses over and over again even if they tell you no I'm not interested. If your fine bugging people on a daily bases as a job then yelp is the job for you.

review_title: Fun work environment but tough job
review_text: Work starts at 8:30AM, I generally get in at 8AM and beginning vetting new business to develop my pipeline. We usually have a meeting at 9AM to discuss what we have going on that day. Depending on my schedule I will either make open calls, pitching business on Yelp ads, or following up with business I have previously pitched. I learned how to maximize my productivity. My goal everyday is to talk on the phone for over 2.5 hours and make over 80 calls. Management is great they are extremely helpful if you have any questions. Anyone from a manager in training to the director of the NYC office will take the time to help you with anything you need. By far the hardest part of the job is not letting a "no" or a bad call affect the rest of your day. I love my co-workers, everyone I work with is great. Such down to earth people. That as well as closing deals is the most enjoyable part of my job for me.

Yelp is great comapny to work for when you're looking to get your foot in the door. The role is essentially a cold-calling position, and after 6 months it wears on you. AEs are expected to make anywhere from 80-100 calls a day to maintain the Yelp machine.

Company culture is fun - very much "work hard, play harder" mentality going on there. Many employees are in their early to mid-twenties.

Because the company's sales org is growing so rapidly, it's easy to fall in between the cracks. If you're a stellar rep, you are constantly rewarded and praised. After time, you'll move up to either management or move to mid-market. Most new managers are either ill equipped or not right for the position based on their personality types. Not everyone can manage.

Be ready to make 70+ outbound calls a day and be on the phones over 2 hours. 

Great training program where you learn how to manipulate language to set appointments and close deals. Was 60 days but recently shortened to 30 days. 

Management is very hit and miss. Some Sr. Management seemed like they just got put into the position cause they were there and Yelp needed someone to step in and manage. Some managers really help develop reps, others just kind of let you sink or swim then cut the fat after you miss quota a few times. 

Culture here is awesome, very young and almost frat like sometimes makes working here fun. You can find so many people into so many different things so its never hard to meet someone with common interest. 


Working with small business owners is a grind. A small percentage of them actually have money to advertise and most of them have a bad taste in their mouths from a previous rep being rude or tasteless when trying to get a deal in. The territories are hard too, sometimes you get a major metro where people use the internet and know Yelp. Other times you end up calling a town with only 20,000 people and no one there even owns a computer. That really screws up you getting a fair shake at the job and can lead to you getting terminated. 

The culture, free beer, parties and people really make the job worth it. Other than that, you don't make a lot of money in a base salary for living in the most expensive housing market in the U.S. People who do well at the job will like it, but there are too many variables that can ruin your experience here.

This company specializes in hiring people in their early 20s living with their parents and with little expectations as far as future and financial planning. They have a pretty nice revolving door going on and they make sure they truly squeeze you real good until they let you go. Benefits do not kick in until 90 days, the leads are old and have been contacted 200 times already.  Managers are out of lower end positions at ilegitimate call centers.
They also discriminate against people of Hispanic culture big time!
Stay away from these idiots. The competition pays better but they are more genuine and human.
surrounded by un educated co-workers and managers.  college kids looking for their first job.

Let me start by saying that the company and culture is amazing at Yelp. My job consisted of setting up advertisements for clients of all types. My manager and co-workers were all very helpful. The job itself can be very rewarding if done correctly. The most enjoyable part of the job was the atmosphere. There is a fully stocked kitchen and things like ping pong and foosball to play in your off time.

review_title: Bad training to sell an even worse product
review_text: You're trained to pressure small business owners into buying the paid version of Yelp. Very high pressure, feels scammy, and management sucks. Wouldn't recommend

The training felt very rushed and lacking in a good foundation for the job. During training you were expected to work  off the clock to practice what you were taught. And the expectation was given that organizational work to be ready for your shift was also outside scheduled work hours.
This was a sales job for ad's but once you sold it to your client you were expected to build a successful ad with them. Even with no understanding of their company.

I think you will be surprised how little money you make even when your sales are high during the training period.  I have worked for companies that really care about their employees, and this was not one of them.

review_title: Good first steps into tech/ advertisement sales.
review_text:
What is the best part of working at the company?
Great training, great benefits. But it's definitely a grind. The pay is  a bit low. Put over all learned a lot and enjoyed my experience there.

What is the most stressful part about working at the company?
Quota is obtainable, but you really have to work for it.

What is the work environment and culture like at the company?
They're definitely on the micromanagement side. Put over all the culture and support is excellent.

What is a typical day like for you at the company?
Typically, there's a morning meeting. Hit your dials. There's another after lunch meeting. Then, some more dails. And hopefully you've pitched twice and closed a deal. Then, the day's over.

Great company for remote sales. It is still cold calling, but as far as that type of work goes it doesn’t get better than Yelp. They provide great on the job training and support for growth as well as great benefits.

review_title: Great place to kick off a career in sales
review_text: If you are kicking off your career in sales, this is a great place to start. The training is thorough. The benefits are next level. Cold calling is not for the faint of heart but this role will give you a great foundation.

review_title: If you can cold call you can make excellent income
review_text: Team meeting in the morning, then hit the phones.  Dials, Dials, Dials,  you must have the dials and a good DM to Pitch and Pitch to Close Ratio if you want to make the big money.    My team was awesome and I enjoyed my time at YELP.   The team celebrates wins and that keeps you motivated.   Training is above average.   The hardest part of the job is cold calling and everything that comes with it.

review_title: Great place to cut your teeth
review_text: For anyone looking to start a career in sales, this is the place to do it. Fantastic training program but brutal day-to-day and near cult-like sales culture. If you can make it selling at Yelp, you'll be able to make it selling anywhere.

Poor commission structure in a company that has lost its integrity and value in the community. Most leads are overused and mistrusting due to the incessant calls they've already received in the past. Management pushes training skills that don't address realistic day to day concerns. The benefits are fantastic, but you are left feeling unfulfilled and not good enough. The trick is though, no one is really good enough and people will start to leave/get fired over time. Lots of bells and whistles and it starts off so great, but the shininess wears off rather quickly.

review_title: Toxic would not recommend working here.
review_text: I work here currently. I hear other departments (other then sales) may love their jb and company but as a sales rep the job is really toxic. You are fearful of losing your position constantly. Their meeting are strange. It's like the supervisor has too give a gold star every 5 minutes. We have 2-3 meetings(trainings) a dy that say the same thing. Close sales BUT the leads are overwork burnt out leads. People who asked Yelp not to call and we still do. People who have been told one thing and charged something else. It is sad but is so micromanaged that it is stressful. The meetings are just weird. It is never enough. Nothing you do is good enough only they tell you this in a passive agressive way. STAY AWAY. It is miserable.

review_title: Best training & PTO , multi task burnout
review_text: If you perform to a high standard here, you’ll make 100k+  first full calendar year. Sales skills required are expected, but multi tasking graphic design, chats, customer tech support can lead to burnout.

They threw us to the wolves after 2 weeks of training and have unrealistic expectations about new hires. You need to perform +80 phone calls a day, followed by 80 emails as well. 
How do they expect you to close sales if some leads are 10 years old? 
The only good part of this company is the benefits, which is one of the best I ever seen.
Good benefits, rough work. Expect to be cold calling 80 or so biz a day, many who have been burned by Yelp in the past. Good training and culture but rough work.

Honestly nothing to complain about the job itself. The training is very in depth and you get the support and tools to succeed. Everybody that you’re calling typically hates Yelp so it’s a constant mental battle. Yes that is just sales but Yelp is something else. There’s not really a community that swear by advertising with Yelp but there is ABSOLUTELY a community that sweats against it. Overall management is great and you have some awesome benefits but  the product itself is a tough one to sell that’s for sure.
Started training this week and I must say I like it so far. Everyone is nice, training is insightful. It seems to be a straightforward sales role with a minimum of 80 calls expected.

review_title: Great first job out of college
review_text:
Some of the best training 
Made great connections and memories
Hard job but learn great sales skills 
Top producers should have bigger increases in their base pay to keep good talent
This job isn't for everyone, don't feel bad if you don't make it more than a year. Enjoy the perks and great benefits and soak up everything you can learn from leadership
Product is dying, have to force it down business owners throat in a one call close; great place to start sales career and make great connections but ship is sinking.

I haven't started training yet but my recruiter has been so helpful! So far they are very responsive and kind. I am ready to learn an be a part of my team and this company! I believe that you have to be able to take feedback and be open to always keep learning.
Great place to start and training is great. Can be a stressful job but management cares and will make sure you are set up for success. Learn a lot of sales and grit.

It’s your average sales position.  Inside sales job, trying to reach stakeholders to sell as buys on their website for businesses.  Management did a good job of supporting sales team and providing training.
One of the best sales training you can get . The leaders and management are great plus the perks were awesome. Great place to grow and plenty of opportunities to move up/

review_title: Decent work, low pay without commissions
review_text: It was overall a decent experience. There’s 2 weeks of training and they train you in detail. The reason I left is because of the commission structure. You have a minimum to sell every mint before you can start to earn commission which is in favorable compared to other sales jobs.

review_title: Great entry level tech job if you are getting started.
review_text: I would say the benefits are pretty good. Base salary could be better but from my experience they do care about your growth and trying to help you succeed. Learned a lot about tech ad sales through cold calling and opens a lot of doors too. Mentioned that you can also move up in the sales career or even go for different roles in the company. Training is probably the toughest part in this role due to getting fed alot of information but the role does get easier as you consistently practice. What is nice about this role is if you get good at it, you definitely can make it a solid career or you can use it for experience and let it open doors for other opportunities. Overall, a pretty good company.

review_title: Great Training, Fabulous Culture, Follow the script, Recycled Leads, great health coverage
review_text: I was an outbound account sales executive with them and it was a positive experience. You called the same leads about 80 or more daily (yelp business leads) over and over for a certain amount of weeks until they assigned you a different set of leads (region). I did get many no answers, bunch of hang ups (hate Yelp) a few live calls that you had to LEAN IN to convert them to sign up for sponsored ad campaign.  Their training did help me become a better one close salesperson. Close them while you have them HOT on the phone. They have a Tiering commission system as you close leads you will ramp up. If you want to become a stronger salesperson and develop thick skin, this is a great place and you will reap the monetary rewards. It takes patience to get there. I was offered another career opportunity that I had acquired my license during my time with Yelp. Otherwise, I would have stayed as I loved the culture, the benefits were awesome, growth opportunities within. They provide work equipment and wfh. Loved it.

Not a helpful or productive work environment. There is barely training and they want you to be an expert right away.  From the upper levels to the lower level they just regurgitate information and without any thought.

review_title: Great environment, not so great management
review_text: This was an interesting place to work. A lot of great amenities, however the training was distasteful. The hardest part of the job was selling the product.

Worked for Yelp doing sales for about 6 months. If you have no experience in sales and want to get started this is a great place to consider. They take people with no experience and provide great training.

review_title: Lots of potential for growth and uncapped commission- comprehensive training and lots of support throughout
review_text: Yelp offers great benefits (including a wellness, childcare, and education credit to use every month) , comprehensive training, and lots of training and support throughout. If you are willing to be taught, take feedback, and continue to learn and grow this is a great position for you. The commission is uncapped and the higher end of the pay rate they offer is definitely attainable. Promotions happen automatically when you make enough sales- so no need to ask for them. During training you just make the base- so the first couple months expect that. There will be some months/days that are harder than others- have to ride ups and downs and build up resiliency in this role. As you advance in the role you are able to make more while selling the same amount. Fully remote on the phone all day making calls. Great opportunity, but not for everyone.

review_title: You have to be ON IT at all times to do well
review_text: The company has a great culture and values. Everyone is very inclusive, but management will be hard on you if you don’t keep up with your dials. You don’t close sales as easily as they make it seem you can during training. This job requires resilience because you are calling business owners that don’t want to talk to you or have had a bad experience with Yelp ads already, but you are still required to sell to them and say all the things you have to say. You must leave a voicemail and an email on every single call. If business owners tell you to stop calling them, management will still force you to call them or else your pipeline will build up. That’s the reality of this job. Closing 1-2 sales a day is considered PRO. It can be soul sucking depending on how you do your job. Good luck.
Excellent training, can definitely learn a lot especially when it comes to closing a sale. However, it’s Selling a bunk product to business owners knowing it won’t help them.
Yelp has a very comprehensive training program and continuous guidance throughout your career. Everyone works remote, so you get to work from the comfort of your own home!

review_title: Dressed Up Nicely - Broiler Room Reality.
review_text: A burning red flag is when 100+ people are hired to start training on the same day.  Plus Side:  Thorough training - Minus Side:  1 call close geared.

Great first job out of college. Great training program. 
Very hard work - cold calling 80 calls a day. Can be very tiring. Some of the management wasn't great.

Great remote culture and leadership is great at being available and helping you with any issue you may have. The pay is very low and your first 3 months you'll be underwater as you go through training (no commish), work your first month, and then wait another 45 days to get paid out. You're judged on how many of the incoming calls you retain, however you dont get a direct line for customers to call in, and the accounts you save will ultimately call in and speak to someone else (acct must retain for 60 days to get paid out on it) and that person they speak will see it's not apart of their books and the account is more likely to cancel. You're paid less than your peers in the field, but if you have the finances to sustain the first 6 months of little to no commision, it's a nice place to work remotely.

Amazing benefits, work-life balance, and supportive environment and team. Ongoing training and potential for career growth. Base salary plus commission, you can decide how much you make and how far you want to go within the company!
Free Red Bulls & snacks. Boiler room sales culture. Your territory will define how much money you make. Capped commissions but great sales training and opportunity to learn how to sell
Working in sales at Yelp was challenging but rewarding. The training process was effective and although the job is mostly cold calling businesses, it felt really rewarding to reach a real person.
Didn’t make it past week of training before quittingâ€¦same to be said for over half my group. Lots of young people and fun seeming office but the job itself just wasn’t what I was looking for.

review_title: Lots of training but high stress environment
review_text: They give you a lot of the tools necessary to succeed. However, it is a high stress environment with high expectations put on each individual to perform.

Amazing opportunity at Yelp, I have nothing bad to say about the company overall 
Amazing sales training. I learnt so much about sales period. Would recommend this company to anyone that is starting out in sales definitely a resume builder
Never should have taken this job, because deep down inside I knew I HATED Yelpers. They feature these Karen-Like individuals in the New Hire Training. I should have ran away then
Great sales training and support opportunities to make great money if you are good at sales.  Must be okay with phone sales / cold calling.  Over 100 dials a day.

review_title: Opportunity of a lifetime for the right person.
review_text:
What is the best part of working at the company?
Culture, training program, ramp up period, bonuses

What is the most stressful part about working at the company?
Following the process aka script

What is the work environment and culture like at the company?
All around great environment for beginners anf pros. Simply need patience within ones self.

What is a typical day like for you at the company?
Research the business, call the business, try to sell the business FAST

review_title: High turnover and management lacks people skillsskills
review_text: Account executive position requires 80 plus calls daily. Most business owners have been called incessantly over and over again. The leads are stale. Half of my training class quit within the first month.

Great work culture until you get out of training. Once out of training expectations are too high with pressure from the higher ups.
Can't imagine how it is virtually, was virtual for about a month and a few weeks until they laid me and 2200 others off.

review_title: Work from home, training one thing expect another. One chance and that is it
review_text: Unless you are a master at cold calling and harassing small/medium size business' for paid advertising you will quickly be asked to live month of training month of learning how to do it make it or don't. If you need to go on a performance plan your management will abandon you.
Met great people, had great management. This job is for people who like sales or aspire to grow in sales. The opportunity is there and it’s what you make it.
Good insurance, have to meet certain sales quotas before you make commission. Training is great and the perks are nice. Gracious time off and great teammates!

The position for an account executive role at Yelp can be a mixed bag. On the one hand, the company provides a great work environment with a supportive team and excellent benefits. However, the job can feel repetitive and even stagnant at times, which may not be ideal for everyone.

As an account executive, your primary role is to develop and maintain relationships with Yelp's clients, which can involve a lot of cold calling and email outreach. While this may be exciting for some, others may find it tedious and monotonous.

One of the benefits of working at Yelp is the opportunity to learn from experienced sales professionals and receive ongoing training and support. However, it's important to note that the company operates in a highly competitive industry, so meeting sales quotas and targets can be challenging and demanding.

Overall, the account executive role at Yelp is a good option for those who enjoy sales and are looking for a dynamic work environment. However, if you're someone who values variety and constant change, this may not be the ideal position for you.

As A Community Ambassador, I am only part time but I could not be more thrilled with my overall experience with this company and I would not hesitate to apply/accept a full time role if a good fit became available. I'd probably even move to work with them full time eventually. They are one of the most inclusive and supportive companies I have ever worked for/with- they do not just support diversity, they actively seek it. My supervisor does a great job encouraging creativity, risk, growth, feedback, praise and autonomy while cultivating a true team and community environment (virtually even)!

What is the best part of working at the company?
Remote work from home and advancement opportunities 

What is the most stressful part about working at the company?
Meeting sales requirements and making 80 plus sales calls per day

What is the work environment and culture like at the company?
Good culture and benefits plus lots of training

What is a typical day like for you at the company?
8 hour day, lots of computer work and making cold calls all day long
They have a good sales training program. But the actual role can be very mundane. Very young workforce, the employees and the management team. Lots of areas for improvement.
Early am shift and weekends off. Great training.You will be micro managed it's part of the development program. 80 dials a day mandatory. GOOD Luck!!!
training set a precedent of what the work would be like, but after 3 months the positivity and fun environment shifts. Best part about the job was as soon as you close your laptop, you're off.

I’m apart of the October Class at Yelp. The training was effective & helpful. They do their best to prepare you for the challenges ahead. However they don’t tell you about the Pitching, Closing, Promotions for Business Owners. 

Just a lot they don’t disclose in your offer letter. You think you’re signing up to do 80 Cold Calls, but it’s recycled leads, you’re encouraged to continue pressing the Business Owner to buy from Yelp when they do not want to. You’re micromanaged A LOT. 

Even when you place someone on a DNC they still pop up in your pipeline. Even when someone has told you â€œNoâ€ multiple times you are encouraged to â€œEVPâ€ (Empathize, Add a Value, Pivot to a computer).

You’re allowed 2, 10min breaks, your calls are tracked & if you don’t talk for 2 hours then you’ll be placed under a microscope. If you don’t hit quota even as a trainee you’ll be put on a performance plan & if you don’t improve you’ll be fired. 

Do your research before making a decision with this company. I love the team environment & the â€œpotentialâ€ to grow, there’s a lot of learning experiences within the position, I personally wouldn’t pursue staying here long term.

Good benefits, good incentives, but not for me.

The training was good, three months. Remote work from home. Positive group and work environment. Low base pay. The job is primarily performance-based with the commission. It would be best if you sold a lot to make commission. Set a schedule highly structured environment. Uses salesforce mostly recycled leads. Work from home but can't choose own work scheduleâ€”good amount of PTO 15 days per year. The quota goes up each month, and after the training ends, you’re mostly on your own, and if you don't hit the min quota, your job is on the chopping block. 70-80 cold calls a day.

review_title: Great team environment, culture, management and training
review_text: Yelp has a training program that is ongoing, and is very well put together.  Overall, the culture and management is are outstanding, second to  none. Super impressed with the training for consultative sales.  Management care about their people and you are constantly asked how u are doing
Great management and training. Awesome benefits and work life balance. The work can be hard sometimes but management will work with you to make sure you see success.
Do your research when applying for AEs at yelp pays below the average but you can expect decent training very flexible hours and ok management staff . Hard expectations

It is cold calling but you have name recognition so it is easier to gain some credibility. The training teaches you absolutely everything you need to know, but you have to be tech savvy, business savvy, and know how to build rapport quicly and think very quickly as to how to keep the conversation going and get biz owners to buy into Yelp. I personally was a top performer and worked there and exceeded sales targets during the pandemic. As long as you keep your call volume high and stick to the script you can do well, not for those who can't take rejection and don't like being on the phones.
The culture is interesting to say the absolute least. It can be a very fun place to work but after training they kinda throw you to the wolves and it very much a sink or swim situation.

I have worked with Yelp now for a few weeks as an account executive in training (I believe that’s what they call it). It’s a cold calling sales job. 

The management with Yelp has been great and I loved working from home however there are really no transferable skills even for an entry level worker in my opinion to gain by working at Yelp. I feel anyone who knows about Yelp would agree that it’s a horrible idea to put on a resume.

They are not teaching sales skills but instead sales script. Yelp requires even the most seasoned and experienced sales people to read from a very badly written script word for word. They claim studies have been done and the script is what works but I find that hard to believe if they recruited better talent and trained sales skills rather then how to read from a page. The unfortunate side is the draw pay is very low and commissions aren’t all that great either so it would be hard to gain good people without paying them better. 

On a positive note the management, IT and all the people who work at Yelp are all very nice! It’s a very all inclusive and accepting company. Yelp also does offer some good perks such as a health and wellness reimbursement. 

For me personally If I were younger and didn’t have any professional sales experience and training maybe this place wouldn’t rub me wrong so badly but having people act as puppets and requiring they say certain things based on a script I feel is actually pretty embarrassing as a company. I am more than confident now if I ever receive a call from a Yelp rep at my business I will defiantly hang up as I know it’s going to be a totally ingenue sales pitch. 

They company as a whole is still gaining in numbers every year the last I heard but I think with all the other marketing and social media platforms available now days Yelp isn’t going to be around in 10 or 20 more years. 

I wish the company luck as they will need it. If you are considering working here I would pass and try to learn how to be a real sales person instead.

I worked at Yelp for a year and a half. It was a great experience and I made some great memories there. I left during the pandemic, because it became hard to sell during that time and management started to micromanage.

Good to learn sales, intensive training is involved. Culture can be a bit off putting, a good amount of work happy hours, office drama, things like that. You can make decent money if you keep hitting your numbers. A good amount of favoritism.

review_title: Fun, engaging and connected place to work.
review_text: Loved how creative you can be and how connected to the community you are. Management was phenomenal as well as training. Compensation lacked and wasn't competitive.

review_title: Great benefits, but will wear you down
review_text: The turnover here is insane. Most people in your training class will leave. The job itself is quite stressful and difficult but some people do make a lot of money.
Selling yelp adds to businesses that don't really want to hear from us . Great insurance and great work life balance . Long training but we need it . So much to learn.

By far the worst place I’ve ever worked remotely. The interview process is them basically pitching you, giving false narratives about the job. The training isn’t as in depth as it should be when it comes to them expecting you to actually sell their products. You’re getting yelled at and bears yes all day on the phones from COLD CALLING people. The management is horrible, don’t know the difference between proper criticism and just being a bully. Constant pressure from them pushing quotas. I would never recommend anyone working here. Run! The pay is bad for the things you do.

review_title: Great PTO. Great benefits with tele health, wellness reimbursement (athletic gear, personal trainer, meal prep, gym membership, etc.) Great training
review_text: Overall it was a great place to work. They recently went fully remote as an organization, and I was part of the first class that was hired directly remote - I felt comfortable getting to know the job from home, but do wish we had a bit more time to put our training to practice before being expected to perform.

The company culture is good. The people you meet and work with is probably the best part of the job. Having said all that, it is a difficult job with 80+ dials a day everyday of cold calling. Not for everyone and its sometimes hard to stay motivated.
It was a great learning experience. Great training program and once you get the courage to leave, you will succeed anywhere you go. Management is great and motivating however high volume dials.
Training was good but you are put on the phone real quick . Supervisors tell you what to say. You have to sell a lot before you are commission eligibl

Overall, this company is fully transparent and effective in its job description and expectations. Each employee has the opportunity to have the type of future they desire with this company through supportive training and management. If you desire a job in sales this is a great company to begin your career.

The Product works for some businesses better than others but they make you pitch it like it works for any business and it doesn't. Pitching  Business Owners that have Been Burned by Yelp in the Past with a new spin on it is always fun..NOTðŸ˜‚
It was a fun job and the culture was great, but the pay was absolutely terrible. The training is great for entry level people but if you have any experience then I do not recommend it.
Great benefits/ran like a well-oiled engine/detailed training &support to perform job/salary +comm/even playing field for all to succeed/room for adva

Yelp is a great company with old dried up leads because they refuse to take no for an answer. So people are tired of hearing from them. You may make 100 calls a day and talk to 2 people. They fired me right before they put most of the company on a temporary lay off. This company is not recession proof as they claim. They rely on businesses to be open. It gets a little tiring when you’re calling people that don’t want to be called no more and you’re being told it’s your fault and your lack of ability. In reality the leads have been the same and called on so many times that they know not to answer. Great culture! Sometimes I felt like they were very cheesy. Making people play games during work.

review_title: Fun Place to work in theory
review_text: Product does not work for every business. Good to have on resume if you can withstand the environment.  I lasted 6 months. I was constantly pulled into meeting rooms to be questioned about my performance. You’re selling Yelp Ads to people who have previously had experience w Yelp ads. In training you get hot leads but as soon as it’s over you get an overworked pipeline. High sellers are considered celebrities

Working in the sales department as an Account Executive is a hit or miss proposition. So much cold-calling with a low success rate - extremely low. Fun environment though. Other departments seem to fare much better.
I love Yelp! Great company, great people, and a great training program. You have PTO and no paid vacation time which I would prefer, but not everything is perfect and Yelp comes pretty close to it
Great company to start sales career or reinvent sales career. Very hands on training for first 2 months teaching you all the ins and outs of the company. Great opportunity for upward mobility.
Appears to be a good company.  Honestly, I was still in training when the Covid-19 situation occurred at which time myself and 50% of all Yelp employees were laid off.

Sales can get real, but Yelp sales is on a whole new level. The only good thing about Yelp is the 2 month training period. The training period feels like you’re being brainwashed. Their sales approach is very aggressive. The product may not necessarily work in the territories it’s being sold. Overall, the best part of this company is developing your communication skills for the good or the bad. Oh the free lunch is eggs and tuna or a cup of noodles.

review_title: The sales roles are challenging, but support is always available.
review_text: The perfect boot camp for sales training.  The role is not for everyone, but any can be successful.  Pay attention to all initial training classes, fail fast, manage up, and learn from your mistakes.

review_title: If you're a high-functioning cool kid, you'll probably be very happy, at least with your paycheck
review_text:
I'd like to preface this by saying that getting to work here was like getting to meet one of my heroes. My delay in realizing why this was a terrible idea probably contributed to my eventual state of disillusionment; I wanted to help, but that wasn't in the description. 

If your clients mean so little to you that you don't mind being utterly worthless to them after closing, this could be a great gig for you.

If you're primarily motivated by money and status/have an easy time being a sociopath, my sympathies friend, you'll probably love it.

Here's the thing; I was a fly on the wall, naturally disappearing into the background, taking notes on everything I saw and heard, because I was hoping it would help me succeed. It didn't, but I'm sharing because I hope it'll help someone else:

-The majority of very successful people (who are called upon to speak almost daily for reasons surpassing understanding) achieve it by exhibiting a *lack* of empathy, however well-intentioned, and not because of it.

-You will, on a daily basis, be expected to plow ahead over a client whether the numbers make sense or not (and you're not expected to know whether they do, more to assume they do).

-You likely won't benefit from trying to learn how to make the data-driven argument, so your integrity might have to be hung up at the door. Making quantifiable evidence scalable and user-friendly just isn't a priority for this organization in any meaningful way.

-You're on an assembly line; it just looks like an office. Expectations will increase, useful training to reach them will not.

-Read all the books and do all the research you want (like I did); having facts isn't what matters to anyone except the clients, and again, you can rarely help them even if you eventually get a yes.

Finally, it was reiterated to me after reporting policy breaches on the phone, that this is a sales organization. Recognizing that poor client retention creates inefficiency and is a waste of everyone's time doesn't happen more than quarterly (when corporate hands down marching orders), and it was personally one of the more painful parts of the job to continue practicing ad infinitum what seemed like such an obviously flawed method of service. Rather than treating leads like gold, they're often spoken to and about like lying fools, in blatant disregard to one of the company values, contributing to my eventual disillusionment. Why would customers be loyal, especially when there's so little transparency and so little effort to improve it?

TL;DR: If you're thinking, "I love Yelp and I love helping people" you may want to reconsider, or be prepared to spend a lot of time not helping anyone, least of all yourself. I learned a lot here; I'd like to unlearn most of it.
A typical day consists of cold calls and conversations with business owners. Throughout my four years at Yelp I have been able to learn to converse with different business and individuals.
Definitely do not recommend if not confident talking on the phone but provides an opportunity to create confidence. Training program is 2 months long - very exceptional
The knowledge, training, and people are what makes this company what it is. If you're unfamiliar with the ad tech space, you'll find yourself learning and excelling quickly here.

review_title: I wouldn't want anyone I care about to work at Yelp.
review_text: When you get out of training it is like completly different company. Super aggressive sales tactics, forced to call business that have requested to be on the DNC and the reps simply dont comply so when you call you get exploded on.  They trap you with benefits and pay you a starting wage that is laughable because they look to hire kids right out of college so they are still living at home. Commision structure is completly busted, you have to selll 43k in revenue for the company to make $84 after taxes. That breaks down to 30k to be commision eligible every month and at least 13k every month to make the minimum of $84. 0 support from upper management/leadership when it comes to customer support, had mutliple accounts just throw money at the wall with problems Yelp could of easily fixed but they were too focused overall on just getting new customers. Super disappointed with how the company was run over all and it was not at all what it was built up to be while in your 2 months of training. Also the fact they say you wont get fired for performance for your first year is true, but they will put you on a performance plan your 12th month and fire you the first day after a year. Dont be fooled, they hire 50 people a month for a reason, the job is terrible and mostly everyone quits. If you read this then get the job ask the tenured reps how they like it. Ask em to be real about it because the whole time I worked there I didnt meet a single person who liked the actual job, just the money you make if you end up sticking it out for about 2 years.

I think that Yelp has a great work environment and good leadership but overall needs more training for employees who have been at the job longer. Once you get past a certain level in the sales role. There is no real outside motivation from the company or management to keep you interested or invested in working there. If you are only money motivated this is the perfect job for you.

review_title: Great place to learn the basics
review_text: Yelp can be brutal, cold calling all day is not easy. However, they have a great sales training program that will teach you the basics of sales. The techniques I learned at help helped launch my sales career.

review_title: You only get out what you put into it
review_text:
You only get out what you put into it

That is really the truth at Yelp. The training there is exceptional and they will really work with you to make you successful. Cold calling sucks but it's somewhere to start where you can make very good money early. Not for the faint of heart. Will be told to harshly screw off while on the acquisition side. This is hard sales but it's a great place to learn to do that well.

review_title: This is a serious job, with serious compensation available
review_text: Great company. Core beliefs are admirable and everything about the company is professional.  Training has to be among the best in the world.  amazing benefits.

review_title: Best Sales training in any company!
review_text:
Yelp trains their employees to be the best salespeople out there.  They are very structured and give guidenace every step of the way.  All companies can take a page out of their guidebook and it really developed me all around.

My sales acumen is owed solely to my development at Yelp.  It was a lot of cold calling the first year but mastering that skill opened new doors to my other roles at the company.

Learned everything thing from Yelp. Awesome sales training program. its a really hard training process and they do let go many people before the end of the training but worth it if you have what it takes to stick around

review_title: Can really go either way and unfortunately it's more luck-based than anything
review_text: Yelp's single biggest flaw from an employee's perspective (and one they've had trouble fixing) is that sales territories are given at random, and while one person who might otherwise be a good salesperson is calling into a small rural town in middle America where people don't rely on a service like Yelp and many don't even have internet access, let alone business competition that would warrant paid advertising, another person who might be a very average salesperson fresh out of college and fresh out of training may be handed a territory in downtown San Francisco or Los Angeles, areas with high Yelp usage, high competition, and a true need for paid advertising. This creates an extremely frustrating work environment.
Great benefits upon hire. Majority of the training class will either leave or be fired after 3 months. You learn a lot of great skills. The job is tough but they want you to succeed.

review_title: It's a fun & young company and people like to have fun
review_text:
I experienced a lot of cold calling, training and talk time.
But have learned the power of email/sms marketing for businesses.
Management is strict and can be stressful.
Most enjoyable thing are my teammates.
Really great culture and awesome training and management team. However if you do not like sales and cold calling this is simply not the job for you...
The job itself is extremely difficult. The training program is incredible. Regardless of if you want to be in sales it is a great place to start a career and build thick skin.

review_title: Fun working environment but the job is metaling draining
review_text: Yelp is great. You get to meet new people that you really hit it off with but the job is draining. It is a glorified telemarketing job. They tend to promote whoever is exceeding quota. I feel like management needs more training. They basically have you trained by new management. It is hard to get the support you need to be successful. I think it is great that they promote from within but the people that are promoted do not have the proper management skills.
phone and computer based position. Good cold calling and negotiation sales training. Upbeat culture and nice perks, along with health and wellness benefits
Yelp is a great company to work for and has an amazing culture. Yelp have an amazing training program and does a good job in embracing the culture. I would recommend.

review_title: Your sales are not real. You are selling yelps web page.
review_text: This is probably the biggest scam next to Google ad words. They will act like it's a great place to work until they split your team up and make you feel uncomfortable.

review_title: Fun workplace/ terrioty dependent on success
review_text:
-Jobs fun ish
-Great training, you can really take away a lot from this job
-Be patient, sales is a process.
-replace don't chase mindset

Overall the experience and culture are 1 of a kind. I only left because I had a more lucrative option but it's a great first step to becoming a successful business person. You learn the market, what works for business's, what doesn't. But that's on you to pay attention too. 

Also the perks are amazing.

Yelp is awesome! Amazing culture, benefits, work-life balance and training. They have an amazing team who really knows how to keep people motivated. 

They just pay nothing to be in a sales role.

review_title: Fun work place, great company culture
review_text: This place is a great place for a first job, great culture and great training. Though you need to be ok with cold calling. The management is great and there is a lot of room for growth

Fun environment with great people
Quotas
Great way to gain experience in sales
Difficult sales process
Great training
Opportunity for advancement
Not for you if you cannot work in a loud office with hundreds of people
Great place to work coming out of college. Sales training is great and you will take it with you in the future. Fun place to work! Not only do you gain great skills you will meet great people.

Yelp is a great place to work, but it's not for everyone. Work is from 8:30-5:30 with overtime rarely required. Management is very supportive for the most part and training is great, but it can lose it's luster doing the same thing every day.
Great training, horrible day to day lifestyle. Basically cold call your life away for over 8 hours a day. Terrible pay, terrible commission, good perks.

New training program is great and will help you overcome objections like a pro, The culture is chill... maybe a little too chill. Great if you are fresh out of college and not willing to let go of your hazing days. If you don't subscribe to sorority/frat culture, in one form or fashion... Good luck

Yelp is a great place to work for anyone who wants to get their feet wet with cold calling and sales. They have a masterful training program that lasts about 3 months. Not to mention an awesome company culture
great company to work for. great training, culture, management and work/life balance. loved working for yelp. would recommend to anyone looking for a sales position.

Fun, tech start up culture. Typical day consists of high volume of outbound calls, prospecting e-mails, demos to closing deals. Work hard, play hard mentality. 

Baristas and stocked kitchens, are a nice perk. Great sense of team camaraderie and training for anyone new to software sales.

Yelp has the worst management I've ever worked under, The experience overall is extremely exciting. The work environment overall is great filled with positive energy. The perks is a free kitchen with a barista, which is awesome. The training program is  in great detail with a lot of information.

Great perks and benefits like a fully stocked kitchen, onsite free barista, kegs in the office, fun culture and management, ping pong tables and young 20 somethings everywhere.

However, cold calling all day making 80+ dials and selling a product/brand that many small business owners seriously do not like. There's no future goal for product innovation to make the ads better for the customer and the main focus is on squeezing every last dollar from a small business owner. They hire recent graduates who have no idea what they're in for and end up firing more than half of them during training.

review_title: Great place to learn the basics of Sales, also a highly competitive environment
review_text: Awesome entry level sales position with amazing training provided. The office is amazing (free snacks, daily lunches, happy hours) and there is a strong sense of "work hard, play hard" amongst employees. Compensation can be tough, but the commission structure is attainable.

review_title: Challenging role within a fun company
review_text: Yelp has a great sales training program and would highly recommend to individuals that want a career in sales. The day to day can be pretty tough, but the atmosphere and the people you work with make it better.  Promotions are plentiful to those that consistently surpass their sales target.

great energy and fun place to work.  Office politics will be the only thing that stops them from taking over the world. 

top notch training  however!
company really values employee happiness and has great benefits. Work like balance is greatly valued. They also have a great training program to prepare you for your role successfully.
Yelp has an extremely fun work environment. Management is great and always helpful. I enjoyed the on-going training and meetings.

review_title: Supportive and fun climate in a demanding role.
review_text: This is definitely a work hard play hard position so if you don't have that kind of work ethic, this isn't for you. But with the extensive training, fun atmosphere and supportive work environment, it's hard to now work hard.

review_title: Fun people but not a ton of room for growth
review_text: Great company that sells a great product, but there's not many interesting positions to move up from entry-level.  Extensive sales training, and excellent benefits.
Very upbeat and exciting company to work for. Amazing training program. Very few people make over $45k, 10% of company stay for over a year.

Yelp is great for entry level professionals who wants to learn sales and account management.  They have an awesome training program.  However, the competitiveness and frat mentality may not be for everyone.
I learned how to talk to small business owners.  I was only there for 3 months because I had to move.  Their sales training is awesome.

review_title: Great work/life balance, Energetic workplace, constant inside training, learning new ways to bring in revenue
review_text:
This was a great opportunity that helped build upon my Sales skills and close business daily.
Through calling businesses I was able to help grow their revenue by bringing in new clients/customers.
Helping Business owners grow their business by showing them the Yelp process, responding to reviews and helping them manage their Yelp Review page.
I enjoy working with small businesses. Work life balance is great. Training tam is always looking to do right by new employees.
Yelp with the 5 Star review! Great culture, Sales Training you couldn't pay for- absolutely one of the best positions for recent grads if you can land yourself a reference or inside interview

review_title: Great company with a strong company culture.
review_text: Strong company culture that permeates all aspects of the job. Management is great, inspiring and helpful but can be very results driven. Wonderful training program, wonderful work environment and awesome benefits but compensation could be better.

role: Ad space sales as Account Executive
review_text:
Incredible environment and training management staff. Just keep in mind this is sales and you must earn your seat.

You work according to the territory you are assigned for 8 hours of cold calls pitches and meetings. 

Fully stocked kitchen even a keg for great End of week celebrations.

Great opportunity for advancement. You can make good money with effort and dedication to the job. It's large corporation with many young adults, for some this can be distracting but if your focused Yelp can be a great place to work.

Management is fair. Some are better than others but the training is the best I've come across.
Good company over all! They have an excellent training program.

Yelp has been such a great experience. The continuous training and work environment are both second to none. 

Walking into an office where everyone is happy to be doing their jobs is unbelievable. One of our mottoes is winning equals fun, but fun does not equal winning. We work in a culture where we celebrate even the smallest victories so as to always keep the energy and attitude up.

My co-workers are my friends. I can't say that for every other job out there.

We sell an emotion-based product, so rejection can be hard to deal with, but it's part of the job. You have to be a professional and move on.
Great culture, very much work hard play hard environment.  Great training program.

review_title: A great place to learn, advance, and grow
review_text:
Yelp is a fun, dynamic place to work. You work closely with management, and there's a lot of transparency with what's going on in the upper levels of the company.

The training is extremely comprehensive and useful. The management provides you the right tools to learn and succeed at your job, and although expectations are high, there's not an unhealthy amount of pressure.

The atmosphere is young, fun, but hardworking -- you are held accountable and to a high standard.

Cold calling, prospecting. You learn to sell thats for sure. The training program is great. The vibe of the office is young and fun, but at the end of the day you still have a headset on in a room with sixty other people with headsets.

The pay is terrible and you need to hit a certain number before you get commission. The best hit that number in three months, the rest take more time. If you want to stick it out with a good company you better have some savings to live off of or live at mom's in the east bay.
